summary: Roland Knyvet Wilson was an Indology scholar who earned his B.A. at the University of Cambridge around 1859 to 1863. He later served at Cambridge as Reader in Indian Law from 1884 to 1893.
Roland Steiner is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied under Michael Hahn. By 2002, he held an assistant professorship at the University of Marburg.

Roland Wenzlhuemer is a historian who earned his doctorate at the University of Salzburg and completed his habilitation at Heidelberg University. He held positions at Heidelberg, the University of Basel, and the University of Munich, where he became director in 2021.

Rolf Alfred Stein was a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology who studied in Paris under teachers including Marcel Granet and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the INALCO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France.

Rolf Hiersche was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena and studied under Richard Karl Heinrich von Kienle. He held posts at Humboldt University, the Free University of Berlin, and the University of Giessen.

Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher. He held academic posts at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Leipzig, Heidelberg, and the University of Munich.

Romain Rolland was a religious studies and philosophy scholar educated at the École Normale Supérieure and the University of Paris. He taught at Lycée Henri-IV, the École Normale Supérieure, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the University of Paris.

Roman Ghirshman was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied in Paris. He directed work at the Musée du Louvre, the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan, and taught at Aix-Marseille University.

Roman Jakobson was a linguist who studied under Wiktor Jan Porzeziński and attended Moscow University and the German University of Prague. He held academic posts at Masaryk University, Harvard University, and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University and completed her doctorate under Arthur Llewellyn Basham at SOAS. She served as a professor at the University of Delhi and Jawaharlal Nehru University.
Ron Garry is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under the traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.
Ronald D. Schwartz is a Tibetology scholar who served as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland and as an Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.
Ronald E. Purser works in religious studies and philosophy and studied under Koshin Ogui. He served on the faculties of Loyola University Chicago and San Francisco State University.

Ronald Egan is a Sinologist who completed his Ph.D. at Harvard University. He held academic positions at Harvard, Wellesley College, the University of California, Santa Barbara, and Stanford University.

Ronald Eric Emmerick was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and Tibetan studies who earned doctorates at Oxford and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey. He held posts at SOAS and was a professor at the University of Hamburg.
Ronald Herman Poelmeijer was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Amsterdam and worked as a lecturer of Tibetan at Leiden University from around 1980 to 1993.
Ronald Inden is an Indologist and historian who spent his career at the University of Chicago, where he became Professor Emeritus of History and South Asian Languages and Civilizations.

Ronald M. Davidson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. He held faculty appointments at California State University, Northridge, and Fairfield University.

Ronald Merry Macphail was an Indology and linguistics scholar educated at The Glasgow Academy and the University of Glasgow. He served with the Church of Scotland and at the Bamdah Medical Mission between 1926 and 1968.
